extracted.intended_audience: graduate students / advanced undergraduates studying algebraic geometry (Math 216 readers)
extracted.subtask_description: A collection of precise criteria, equivalent characterizations, and consequences for flatness, smoothness, étaleness, and related notions (slicing/Tor criteria, fibral flatness, constancy results in flat families, and formal lifting definitions). Geared to users proving or checking these properties in algebraic-geometry problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tor comparison under non-zerodivisor slicing (Lemma 24.6.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: Suppose M is a B-module and t ∈ B is not a zerodivisor on M. Then for any B/(t)-module N, one has Tor^B_i(M, N) = Tor^{B/(t)}_i(M/tM, N).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof by taking a free resolution of M, reducing modulo t (uses that t is not a zerodivisor to ensure vanishing of higher Tori with B/(t)), and comparing the complexes; useful to deduce flatness of M from flatness of M/tM under the non-zerodivisor hypothesis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local criterion for flatness (Theorem 24.6.2) [referenced]
rubrics_metrics.description: Flatness can be detected locally via vanishing of Tor modules (used in text as: by the local criterion we know Tor^B_1(M,B/n)=0).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used repeatedly: to check flatness one reduces to Tor_1 vanishing with residue fields/modules. (The detailed statement is in Theorem 24.6.2; the text uses it as a standard test in proofs and exercises.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Slicing criterion for flatness in the source (Exercise 24.6.G)
rubrics_metrics.description: Suppose A is a B-algebra, A and B Noetherian, M is a finitely generated A-module, and f ∈ A has the property that for all maximal ideals m ⊂ B, multiplication by f is injective on M/mM. If M is B-flat then M/fM is also B-flat.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hint: use the local criterion for flatness (Theorem 24.6.2). Geometric interpretation: relative effective Cartier divisors in flat families are flat on the base; used to show relative Cartier divisors remain flat when the family is flat.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local slicing criterion for flatness without Noetherian hypotheses (Remark 24.6.7)
rubrics_metrics.description: Noetherian hypotheses in Exercise 24.6.G can be removed: if (B,n)→(A,m) is a flat local homomorphism and A is the localization of a finitely presented B-algebra, and if f ∈ A is a nonzero divisor in A/mA, then A/f is flat over B.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reference given: Stacks Project tag 046Z. Use when working outside Noetherian hypotheses but with essentially finite presentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fibral Flatness Theorem (24.6.9)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a commuting diagram X --π--> Y and X --τ--> Z --ρ--> Y with a finitely presented quasicoherent sheaf F on X and points p∈X, q=π(p)∈Z, r=τ(p)∈Y, under hypotheses (X,Y locally Noetherian or ρ,τ locally of finite presentation) the following are equivalent: (a) F is τ-flat at p and F|_r is π_r-flat at p; (b) ρ is flat at q and F is π-flat at p.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provides a practical criterion to deduce π-flatness by factoring through a flat map ρ and checking fibral flatness; proof strategy: reduce to affine case, reduce to Noetherian situation, then solve commutative-algebra problem (EGA reference).

rubrics_metrics.name: Euler characteristic is locally constant in flat projective families (Theorem 24.7.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: If π:X→Y is a projective morphism of locally Noetherian schemes and F is a coherent sheaf on X flat over Y, then χ(X_q, F|_{X_q}) = Σ_{i≥0} (-1)^i dim_{κ(q)} H^i(X_q, F|_{X_q}) is a locally constant function of q∈Y.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof outline: reduce to X = P^n_B and twist by O(m) for m ≫ 0 to kill higher pushforwards; use the Cech complex whose terms are flat to conclude π_*F(m) is flat and hence locally free, so ranks (h^0) are locally constant; Euler characteristic follows. This theorem gives necessary conditions for flatness and leads to many geometric consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hilbert polynomial constancy (Corollary 24.7.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the hypotheses of Theorem 24.7.1, the Hilbert polynomial of F|_{X_q} is locally constant as a function of q∈Y.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Immediate corollary because Hilbert polynomial is determined by sufficiently large twists where cohomology vanishing and local-freeness apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Degree of an invertible sheaf constant in flat families of curves (Corollary 24.7.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: If π:X→Y is a flat projective family of curves and L is an invertible sheaf on X, then the degree of L|_{X_q} on the fibers is a locally constant function of q∈Y.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because invertible sheaves are flat and Euler characteristics are constant in flat families, degrees (defined via Euler characteristic for curves) are constant on fibers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intersection numbers locally constant in flat families (Exercise 24.7.D)
rubrics_metrics.description: If π:X→Y is proper to a connected scheme, L1,...,Ln are line bundles on X, and F is a coherent sheaf on X flat over Y whose support on every fiber has dimension ≤ n, then the intersection numbers (L1...Ln · F)_q on fibers are independent of q.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Starred exercise generalizing constancy results; uses flatness and properness hypotheses and intersection theory (see Chapter 20 references).

rubrics_metrics.name: Algebraic equivalence of line bundles (Definition 24.7.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Line bundles L1 and L2 on a k-variety X are algebraically equivalent if there exists a connected k-variety Y with two k-points q1,q2 and a line bundle L on X×Y whose restrictions to fibers over q1 and q2 are isomorphic to L1 and L2 respectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This gives the subgroup Pic^0 X of line bundles algebraically equivalent to O_X and leads to the Néron–Severi group Pic X / Pic^0 X; constancy-of-degree results motivate these notions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Desired alternate definitions: smoothness and étaleness (25.1.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Candidate (equivalent) definitions: (smooth) π:X→Y smooth of relative dimension n iff (i) π locally of finite presentation, (ii) π flat of relative dimension n, and (iii) Ω_{X/Y} locally free of rank n. (étale) π is étale iff π locally of finite presentation, flat, and Ω_{X/Y}=0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are the geometric/alternate characterizations that will be shown equivalent to the earlier Definition 12.6.2 in Theorem 25.2.2 and Exercise 25.2.B respectively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equivalent characterizations of smooth morphisms (Theorem 25.2.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: For π:X→Y a morphism of schemes the following are equivalent: (i) π is smooth of relative dimension n (Def.12.6.2); (ii) π locally finitely presented and flat of relative dim n, and Ω_π locally free of rank n; (iii) π locally finitely presented and flat and fibers are smooth varieties of dimension n; (iv) π locally finitely presented and flat and geometric fibers are smooth varieties of dimension n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The theorem ties together local presentation, flatness, behavior of Ω, and smoothness of (geometric) fibers; proof strategy involves localization, base-change to fields, Jacobian criterion, slicing and Nakayama arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Étale equivalence formulations (Exercise 25.2.C and 25.2.B)
rubrics_metrics.description: Equivalent ways to state that π is étale: (a) π is étale (Def.12.6.2); (b) π is smooth and unramified; (c) π locally finitely presented, flat, and unramified; (d) π locally finitely presented, flat, and for each q∈Y, π^{-1}(q) is a disjoint union of Spec K where K/κ(q) are finite separable extensions; (e) geometric fiber condition (disjoint union of copies of the geometric point).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These equivalences show étale maps are precisely flat, locally of finite presentation maps with trivial relative differentials (and finite separable fiber structure).

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal smoothness/unramified/étale via infinitesimal lifting (Definition 25.2.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: π:X→Y is formally smooth (resp. formally étale, formally unramified) if for all affine Z and every closed subscheme Z_0⊂Z defined by a nilpotent ideal, the canonical map Hom_Y(Z, X) → Hom_Y(Z_0, X) is surjective (resp. bijective, injective).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the EGA/Stacks-style infinitesimal lifting criterion; one recovers smooth/étale/unramified by adding finiteness hypotheses (locally of finite presentation). References: EGA IV and Stacks tags cited in the text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Smooth ⇒ flat (Exercise 25.2.A)
rubrics_metrics.description: If π:X→Y is smooth of relative dimension n (with either Y locally Noetherian or using the non-Noetherian slicing remark), then π is flat.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hint: locally express π as Spec B[x_1,...,x_{n+r}]/(f1,...,fr) → Spec B and use induction and the slicing criterion for flatness in the source.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generic smoothness on the source (Theorem 25.3.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let k be a field of characteristic 0 and π:X→Y a dominant morphism of integral k-varieties. Then there is a nonempty dense open U⊂X such that π|_U is smooth of dimension dim X − dim Y.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses transcendence-degree computation to get rank of Ω_{X/Y} at the generic point, upper semicontinuity of fiber rank to obtain a dense open where Ω has the expected rank, and generic flatness to ensure flatness on an open set.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generic smoothness in the target (Theorem 25.3.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: If π:X→Y is a morphism of k-varieties (char k = 0) with X smooth, then there exists a dense open U⊂Y such that π|_{π^{-1}(U)} is a smooth morphism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A complementary generic-smoothness statement useful when the source is already smooth; proof uses rank/determinantal considerations and a lemma bounding dimensions of images of rank loci.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rank condition implies dimension bound (Lemma 25.3.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: For finite type schemes over a field k (char 0) and π:X→Y, define X_r = { p ∈ X : rank(π^*Ω_{Y/k} → Ω_{X/k})|_p ≤ r }. Then dim π(X_r) ≤ r.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interprets rank of the cotangent map as rank of the tangent map; used to deduce generic smoothness in the target. Exercise: show π(X_r) is constructible so its dimension makes sense.
